A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and 15-page appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite pagination and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original CARLA experiments evaluating infrastructure-taught detection, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, domain adaptation, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a filtering ablation and a real-world UrbanIng-V2X adaptation experiment.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, Algorithm 1, RSU pseudo-label generation, tracking, filtering, aggregation, and ego training remain unchanged. Removing filtering is tested as an ablation, not adopted as a revised method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only the simulated CIVET environments. Appendix D.2 of v2 adds actual evaluation on UrbanIng-V2X through cross-intersection adaptation, substantially extending coverage from simulation to real-world data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including MODEST and Oyster in Table 5 and the supervised-RSU and ego-ground-truth controls. The added real-world study reuses unadapted-ego and supervised/unsupervised-RSU comparison approaches.

E3.justification: The added real-world experiment pretrains on all intersections except the target, then adapts to that target and reports dynamic-object AP at IoU 0.3. Existing CIVET splits, sensors, training budgets, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 adds an ablation testing whether broadcast pseudo-label filtering matters. Appendix D.2 also adds a preliminary cross-intersection adaptation check; existing noise, tracking, placement, distance, and RSU-sharing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these results. v2 adds no uncertainty estimates or seed information for its new experiments.

E6.justification: Existing table values and figure results are unchanged. v2 adds AP of 60.0 without filtering versus 66.4 for Table 1 row ❹. Its new UrbanIng-V2X experiment reports 23.5 before adaptation, 29.3 with supervised RSU labels, and 24.8 with unsupervised labels at IoU 0.3.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation and assumptions are retained. No definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: infrastructure-taught label-free learning, a standalone ego detector, and a feasibility study demonstrating scalability and complementarity. The new evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 newly interprets the real-world results as evidence that broadcasting transfers to real data and attributes the weaker unsupervised result to MODEST's difficulty with stationary objects such as parked cars. Section 3.2 also explicitly emphasizes feasibility over individual-module innovation.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, training schedules, and hardware. The project-page address is unchanged; the new real-world paragraph adds evaluation design but no implementation or resource-access details.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 84 works and retain their positioning relative to collaborative perception and ego-centric label-free learning. UrbanIng-V2X and MODEST were already cited; added bibliography backlinks are formatting changes.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose additions, grammatical corrections, and header and acknowledgement edits. The overall section organization and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables retain their content. Figures 7–8 move from page 13 to page 14, appendix material reflows, and v2 changes affiliation formatting and adds colored citation links and bibliography backlinks.

improvement.justification: The filtering ablation supports an existing design choice, while the UrbanIng-V2X experiment provides initial evidence beyond v1's simulation-only evaluation. These gains are limited: the real-world protocol is briefly documented, uncertainty is unreported, and unsupervised adaptation reaches only 24.8 AP from 23.5, versus 29.3 with supervised RSU labels. The additions strengthen the paper modestly without establishing comprehensive real-world label-free effectiveness.
